608	# ─── _cycle_stash_predicate — record last predicate eval for OUTPUT banner ───
609	# #833: the cycle OUTPUT banner restates the most-recently evaluated
610	# termination predicate. Both _cycle_check_until and _cycle_check_abort_when
611	# already compute kind/stage/field/op/expected/actual/match; stash them here so
612	# _cycle_render_predicate_result can format them without recomputation.
613	_cycle_stash_predicate() {

615	    _CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_STAGE="$2"
616	    _CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_FIELD="$3"
617	    _CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_OP="$4"
618	    _CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_EXPECTED="$5"
619	    _CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_ACTUAL="$6"
620	    _CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_MATCH="$7"
621	}

623	# ─── _cycle_render_feedback_digest <iter> <state_dir> (#833) ─────────────────
624	# The cycle INPUT-banner body. iter==1 → "(no feedback — first iteration)";
625	# later iterations → how many stage summaries the next stage's Previous work
626	# carries (#2124). Read-only, never trips errexit.
627	_cycle_render_feedback_digest() {
628	    local iter="$1" state_dir="$2"
629	    if [[ "$iter" == "1" ]]; then
630	        printf '(no feedback — first iteration)'
631	        return 0
632	    fi
633	    _cycle_render_summaries_digest "$state_dir"
634	}

636	# _cycle_render_summaries_digest <state_dir> (#2124) — how many stage summaries
637	# the next stage's Previous work carries, and how many of those stages failed.
638	_cycle_render_summaries_digest() {
639	    local state_dir="$1" counts n r
640	    if ! declare -F stage_summaries_count >/dev/null 2>&1; then
641	        # shellcheck source=./input-resolve.sh
642	        source "$_CYCLE_ORCH_ROOT/core/pipeline/input-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
643	    fi
644	    counts="$(stage_summaries_count "$state_dir/pipeline-state.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"
645	    n="${counts% *}"; r="${counts##* }"
646	    [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || n=0
647	    [[ "$r" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || r=0
648	    if [[ "$n" -eq 0 ]]; then
649	        printf '(no stage summaries)'
650	    else
651	        printf 'summaries(%s stage summaries, %s failing)' "$n" "$r"
652	    fi
653	    return 0
654	}

656	# ─── _cycle_read_progress <state_dir> (#1243) ────────────────────────────────
657	# Code-change PROGRESS axis for the cycle health score: the changes the members
658	# of ONE iteration reported (#2189 — the verdicts blob, not a stage's file),
659	# echoed as "<files_changed> <lines_added> <lines_removed>". No report, or a
660	# cycle whose members change nothing, reads as "0 0 0" (→ "no progress").
661	_cycle_read_progress() {
662	    local blob="${1:-}"
663	    [[ -n "$blob" ]] || blob='{}'
664	    local out
665	    out="$(jq -r '
666	        [ .[]? | (.report.changes // empty) ] as $cs
667	        | ([ $cs[] | (.files // [])[] ] | unique | length) as $f
668	        | ([ $cs[] | (.added // 0) ] | add // 0) as $a
669	        | ([ $cs[] | (.removed // 0) ] | add // 0) as $r
670	        | "\($f) \($a) \($r)"' <<< "$blob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
671	    local files add del
672	    read -r files add del <<< "$out"
673	    [[ "$files" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || files=0
674	    [[ "$add"   =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || add=0
675	    [[ "$del"   =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || del=0
676	    printf '%s %s %s' "$files" "$add" "$del"
677	    return 0
678	}

716	# ─── _cycle_render_predicate_result <iter> [state_dir] (#833, #1241, #1243) ───
717	# Builds the cycle OUTPUT-banner body from the last-stashed predicate eval:
718	#   line1: <kind> stage=<s> field=<f> op=<op> value=<v> → MATCHED|NOT MATCHED (got=<actual>)
719	#   line2 (#1243): multi-axis health score, human-readable, calculation shown.
720	#   line3 (#1241, NOT MATCHED only): failed gates: <list>[ — <reason>]
721	# #1243: the old single-axis `velocity=0-fc` was misleading — an iteration that
722	# applied ZERO code read only as "more defects". The health line now combines
723	# two axes into one total with the arithmetic visible:
724	#   code-change PROGRESS (lines_added+lines_removed this iter) − DEFECTS (fc)
725	#     → SCORE. A zero-diff iter explicitly reads "no progress" (distinct from a
726	#   regression).
727	# #1241: the optional <state_dir> lets the banner name what blocked (not just
728	# "NOT MATCHED (got=fail)"); omitted → no failed-gates line. Pure/read-only; no errexit hazard.
729	_cycle_render_predicate_result() {
730	    local iter="$1"
731	    local state_dir="${2:-}"
732	    local kind="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_KIND:-exit_when}"
733	    local stage="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_STAGE:-}"
734	    local field="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_FIELD:-}"
735	    local op="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_OP:-}"
736	    local expected="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_EXPECTED:-}"
737	    local actual="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_ACTUAL:-}"
738	    local match="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_MATCH:-false}"
739	    local fc="${_CYCLE_LAST_FAILURE_COUNT:-0}"
740	    [[ "$fc" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || fc=0
741	    local matched_str="NOT MATCHED (got=${actual})"
742	    [[ "$match" == "true" ]] && matched_str="MATCHED (got=${actual})"
743	
744	    local files add del
745	    read -r files add del <<< "$(_cycle_read_progress "${_CYCLE_LAST_VERDICTS_BLOB:-}")"
746	    local progress=$(( add + del ))
747	    local score=$(( progress - fc ))
748	    local health_line
749	    if [[ "$progress" -eq 0 ]]; then
750	        # Zero forward code change — surface it as a distinct signal from defects.
751	        health_line="$(printf 'health: progress=0 (no progress) - defects=%s → score=%s' "$fc" "$score")"
752	    else
753	        health_line="$(printf 'health: progress=%s (%s files, +%s/-%s) - defects=%s → score=%s' \
754	            "$progress" "$files" "$add" "$del" "$fc" "$score")"
755	    fi
756	    printf '%s stage=%s field=%s op=%s value=%s → %s\n%s' \
757	        "$kind" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "$matched_str" \
758	        "$health_line"
759	    # #1241: on a NOT-MATCHED terminating iter, name the failing gate(s) + reason
760	    # so the operator sees the cause. A pass
761	    # (MATCHED) is never annotated with failures. Best-effort/read-only.
762	    # #2189: what the cycle's own exit_when stage reported this iteration.
763	    local _u_stage="${_CYCLE_LAST_PREDICATE_STAGE:-${_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE:-}}"
764	    if [[ "$match" != "true" && -n "$state_dir" && -n "$_u_stage" ]]; then
765	        local _failed _reason
766	        _failed="$(jq -r --arg u "$_u_stage" '(.[$u].report.failed_items // []) | join(", ")' <<< "${_CYCLE_LAST_VERDICTS_BLOB:-\{\}}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
767	        _reason="$(jq -r --arg u "$_u_stage" '.[$u].report.reason // empty' <<< "${_CYCLE_LAST_VERDICTS_BLOB:-\{\}}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
768	        if [[ -n "$_failed" ]]; then
769	            printf '\nfailed gates: %s' "$_failed"
770	            [[ -n "$_reason" ]] && printf ' — %s' "$_reason"
771	        fi
772	    fi
773	    return 0
774	}

776	# ─── _cycle_check_abort_when <verdicts_blob> ─────────────────────────────────
777	# ADR-027 (Wave 17-B #703). Mirrors _cycle_check_until against the per-cycle
778	# _TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_* fields. Returns 0 if predicate fired (abort), else 1.
779	# Missing field → 1 (NEVER spuriously abort). No event-emit here — the caller
780	# in cycle_orchestrator_run emits cycle.complete reason=cycle_abort via the
781	# terminal fan-in.
782	_cycle_check_abort_when() {
783	    local blob="$1"
784	    local safe="${_CYCLE_TRAP_CYCLE_ID//-/_}"
785	    local stage_var="_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_STAGE_${safe}"
786	    local stage="${!stage_var:-}"
787	    local field_var="_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_FIELD_${safe}"
788	    local field="${!field_var:-}"
789	    local op_var="_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_OP_${safe}"
790	    local op="${!op_var:-}"
791	    local val_var="_TPL_CYCLE_ABORT_WHEN_VALUE_${safe}"
792	    local expected="${!val_var:-}"
793	    [[ -z "$stage" || -z "$field" || -z "$op" || -z "$expected" ]] && return 1
794	    local actual
795	    actual="$(jq -r --arg s "$stage" --arg f "$field" \
796	        '.[$s][$f] // empty' <<< "$blob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
797	    if [[ -z "$actual" || "$actual" == "null" ]]; then
798	        _cycle_emit_predicate "abort_when" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "" "false"
799	        # #833 NOTE #2: do NOT overwrite the predicate stash here — abort_when
800	        # did not fire (missing actual), so the cycle OUTPUT banner must keep
801	        # showing the exit_when evaluation _cycle_check_until already stashed.
802	        return 1
803	    fi
804	    local _match="false"
805	    local _rc=1
806	    case "$op" in
807	        eq) [[ "$actual" == "$expected" ]] && { _match="true"; _rc=0; } ;;
808	        ne) [[ "$actual" != "$expected" ]] && { _match="true"; _rc=0; } ;;
809	        # #1987: `in` matches any member of a space-separated set. Added because
810	        # a closed vocabulary makes one-of genuinely necessary — two fault
811	        # classes can share a destination, and expressing that as two edges
812	        # needs a list grammar this parser does not have. `eq`/`ne` are
813	        # unchanged, so every existing predicate behaves identically.
814	        in) [[ " $expected " == *" $actual "* ]] && { _match="true"; _rc=0; } ;;
815	    esac
816	    _cycle_emit_predicate "abort_when" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "$actual" "$_match"
817	    # #833 NOTE #2: only let abort_when overwrite the OUTPUT-banner predicate
818	    # stash when it ACTUALLY matched (the terminating predicate). On a normal /
819	    # converged iter, abort_when evaluates to NOT MATCHED — leaving its eval in
820	    # the stash would mis-render the banner as `abort_when ... NOT MATCHED`
821	    # instead of the exit_when evaluation that actually drove the iteration.
822	    if [[ "$_match" == "true" ]]; then
823	        _cycle_stash_predicate "abort_when" "$stage" "$field" "$op" "$expected" "$actual" "$_match"
824	    fi
825	    return $_rc
826	}

833	        _cycle_emit "cycle.metric.invalid" "iter=$iter" "max=$max" \

840	# ─── _cycle_detect_plateau <history_file> <window> ───────────────────────────
841	# N consecutive iterations with identical verdict tuple → plateau.
842	# Skip + emit cycle.plateau.skipped when iter<2 OR history_lines<N.
843	_cycle_detect_plateau() {
844	    local history_file="$1" window="$2"
845	    if ! [[ "$window" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$window" -lt 2 ]]; then
846	        _cycle_emit "cycle.metric.invalid" "metric=plateau_window" "value=$window"
847	        return 1
848	    fi
849	    if [[ "$_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER" -lt 2 ]]; then
850	        _cycle_emit "cycle.plateau.skipped" "iter=$_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER" \
851	            "reason=insufficient_history"
852	        return 1
853	    fi
854	    local lines=0
855	    [[ -f "$history_file" ]] && lines="$(wc -l 2>/dev/null < "$history_file" | tr -d ' ')"
856	    if ! [[ "$lines" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$lines" -lt "$window" ]]; then
857	        _cycle_emit "cycle.plateau.skipped" "iter=$_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER" \
858	            "reason=insufficient_history" "have=$lines" "need=$window"
859	        return 1
860	    fi
861	    # Examine last `window` rows. Plateau if all verdict tuples are identical.
862	    local tail_rows; tail_rows="$(tail -n "$window" "$history_file" 2>/dev/null)"
863	    local distinct
864	    distinct="$(printf '%s\n' "$tail_rows" | jq -r '"\(.verdict)|\(.status)|\(.failure_count)"' 2>/dev/null | sort -u | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
865	    if [[ "$distinct" == "1" ]]; then
866	        _CYCLE_LAST_PLATEAU_EVIDENCE="verdict_tuple_identical"
867	        return 0
868	    fi
869	    return 1
870	}

872	# ─── _cycle_detect_velocity_plateau <history_file> <window> ──────────────────
873	# No consecutive pair in the last <window> failure_counts shows a decrease →
874	# velocity plateau (flat or worsening). Fires BEFORE max_iterations (priority
875	# 1.5) so a stalled cycle exits early without consuming all iterations.
876	# Skip + emit cycle.plateau.skipped when iter<2 OR history_lines<window.
877	_cycle_detect_velocity_plateau() {
878	    local history_file="$1" window="$2"
879	    # window=0 means the feature is disabled (no velocity_plateau.window in template).
880	    [[ "$window" -eq 0 ]] 2>/dev/null && return 1
881	    if ! [[ "$window" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$window" -lt 2 ]]; then
882	        _cycle_emit "cycle.metric.invalid" "metric=velocity_plateau_window" "value=$window"
883	        return 1
884	    fi
885	    if [[ "$_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER" -lt 2 ]]; then
886	        _cycle_emit "cycle.plateau.skipped" "iter=$_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER" \
887	            "reason=insufficient_history"
888	        return 1
889	    fi
890	    local lines=0
891	    [[ -f "$history_file" ]] && lines="$(wc -l 2>/dev/null < "$history_file" | tr -d ' ')"
892	    if ! [[ "$lines" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$lines" -lt "$window" ]]; then
893	        _cycle_emit "cycle.plateau.skipped" "iter=$_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER" \
894	            "reason=insufficient_history" "have=$lines" "need=$window"
895	        return 1
896	    fi
897	    # Tail the last <window> rows; extract failure_count values.
898	    local tail_rows; tail_rows="$(tail -n "$window" "$history_file" 2>/dev/null)"
899	    local -a fcs=()
900	    local row
901	    while IFS= read -r row; do
902	        local fc; fc="$(jq -r '.failure_count // 0' <<< "$row" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")"
903	        fcs+=("$fc")
904	    done <<< "$tail_rows"
905	    # Plateau if no consecutive pair shows a strict decrease (fc[i] > fc[i+1]).
906	    local i
907	    for (( i=0; i < ${#fcs[@]} - 1; i++ )); do
908	        if (( ${fcs[$i]} > ${fcs[$(( i + 1 ))]} )) 2>/dev/null; then
909	            return 1  # found a decrease → not a velocity plateau
910	        fi
911	    done
912	    _CYCLE_LAST_PLATEAU_EVIDENCE="velocity_flat"
913	    return 0
914	}

916	# ─── _cycle_detect_blocked <verdicts_blob> <iter> ────────────────────────────
917	# #528 — early-abort when any stage in _CYCLE_STAGES[] this iter has raw
918	# verdict ∈ {error, corrupt_diff, block} (the "cannot-recover" class).
919	#
920	# Returns: 0 = blocked (terminate-now), 1 = not blocked.
921	#
922	# Pin (silent-failure CRITICAL #1): blocked = verdict-PRESENT + value-in-set.
923	#   verdict=missing is handled exclusively by cycle.iteration.verdict_missing
924	#   emitted from _cycle_check_until — DO NOT double-emit.
925	# Pin (silent-failure CRITICAL #2).
926	#   Blocked fires on verdict; feedback.missing fires on missing-artifact.
927	# Pin (silent-failure HIGH #5): no debounce — these are structural failures
928	#   (corrupt patch, dispatch error) and retry doesn't help. EXCEPT: bypass
929	#   blocked when _CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE == "error" (operator template explicitly
930	#   converging on error).
931	# Pin (silent-failure HIGH #6): jq parse failure OR empty blob → fail-CLOSED,
932	#   treat as terminate-now (mirrors _cycle_check_max_iterations non-numeric).
933	# Pin (HIGH #7): read from $1 (caller passes _CYCLE_LAST_VERDICTS_BLOB), NEVER
934	#   from history — resume-safe by construction.
935	_cycle_detect_blocked() {
936	    local blob="$1" iter="$2"
937	    # Operator-bypass: if until-value is explicitly "error", the template is
938	    # converging ON error — let until fire, don't shadow it.
939	    # #1284: for multi-condition, bypass if ANY condition targets "error".
940	    if [[ "${_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE:-}" == "error" ]]; then
941	        return 1
942	    fi
943	    if [[ -n "${_CYCLE_EXIT_COMBINATOR:-}" ]]; then
944	        local _ew_c
945	        for _ew_c in "${_CYCLE_EXIT_CONDITIONS[@]}"; do
946	            [[ "${_ew_c##*|}" == "error" ]] && return 1
947	        done
948	    fi
949	    # Fail-CLOSED: empty / unset blob.
950	    if [[ -z "$blob" || "$blob" == "{}" ]]; then
951	        _cycle_emit "cycle.metric.invalid" "metric=verdicts_blob_empty" \
952	            "iter=$iter"
953	        return 0
954	    fi
955	    # Fail-CLOSED: jq parse failure on the blob itself.
956	    if ! jq -e . <<< "$blob" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
957	        _cycle_emit "cycle.metric.invalid" "metric=blocked_eval" \
958	            "iter=$iter" "reason=jq_failed"
959	        return 0
960	    fi
961	    local s v
962	    for s in "${_CYCLE_STAGES[@]}"; do
963	        v="$(jq -r --arg s "$s" '.[$s].verdict // empty' <<< "$blob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
964	        case "$v" in
965	            error|corrupt_diff|block)
966	                # ADR-029 G2 (#810): a verdict=error from this iter that
967	                # came from a router timeout/OOM is recoverable — the
968	                # member loop's G2 logic owns the abandon decision and
969	                # already terminated rc=4 if it hit threshold. If we
970	                # reached _cycle_detect_blocked, the counter is still
971	                # under threshold, so let the cycle iterate once more.
972	                # Without this skip, the first verdict=error would
973	                # always shadow G2's count-to-2 rule.
974	                if [[ "$v" == "error" ]] && \
975	                   [[ -n "${_CYCLE_TIMEOUT_RUN[$s]:-}" ]] && \
976	                   [[ "${_CYCLE_TIMEOUT_RUN[$s]}" -ge 1 ]]; then
977	                    continue
978	                fi
979	                # Stash matched stage/verdict so caller can emit cycle.blocked
980	                # with the originating context (event ordering MED #9).
981	                _CYCLE_BLOCKED_STAGE="$s"
982	                _CYCLE_BLOCKED_VERDICT="$v"
983	                return 0
984	                ;;
985	        esac
986	    done
987	    return 1
988	}

990	# ─── _cycle_detect_divergence <history_file> <K> ─────────────────────────────
991	# K consecutive POSITIVE failure_count deltas → divergence.
992	# Skip when iter<K+1.
993	_cycle_detect_divergence() {
994	    local history_file="$1" k="$2"
995	    if ! [[ "$k" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$k" -lt 1 ]]; then
996	        _cycle_emit "cycle.metric.invalid" "metric=divergence_window" "value=$k"
997	        return 1
998	    fi
999	    if [[ "$_CYCLE_TRAP_ITER" -lt $(( k + 1 )) ]]; then
1000	        return 1
1001	    fi
1002	    local lines=0
1003	    [[ -f "$history_file" ]] && lines="$(wc -l 2>/dev/null < "$history_file" | tr -d ' ')"
1004	    if ! [[ "$lines" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$lines" -lt $(( k + 1 )) ]]; then
1005	        return 1
1006	    fi
1007	    # Tail K+1 failure_counts; check K consecutive positive deltas.
1008	    local tail_rows; tail_rows="$(tail -n $(( k + 1 )) "$history_file" 2>/dev/null)"
1009	    local -a fcs=()
1010	    local row
1011	    while IFS= read -r row; do
1012	        local v; v="$(jq -r '.failure_count // 0' <<< "$row" 2>/dev/null)"
1013	        if ! [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
1014	            _cycle_emit "cycle.metric.invalid" "metric=failure_count" "value=$v"
1015	            return 1
1016	        fi
1017	        fcs+=("$v")
1018	    done <<< "$tail_rows"
1019	    [[ ${#fcs[@]} -lt $(( k + 1 )) ]] && return 1
1020	    local i
1021	    for (( i=1; i<${#fcs[@]}; i++ )); do
1022	        local prev="${fcs[$(( i - 1 ))]}" cur="${fcs[$i]}"
1023	        if (( cur - prev <= 0 )); then
1024	            return 1
1025	        fi
1026	    done
1027	    return 0
1028	}

1030	# ─── _cycle_resolve_scope_expansion <cycle_id> <state_dir> (#840 / ADR-030) ──
1031	# Reads a scope_expansion_request emitted by a member (build-summary.json),
1032	# resolves it against the cycle's scope_policy via scripts/lib/scope-governance.sh,
1033	# and acts. Echoes the decision: none | grant | deny.
1034	#   grant   → granted paths written to <state_dir>/scope-expansion-grant.txt and
1035	#             exported as ZBUILD_SCOPE_EXPANSION_GRANT (build merges it next iter);
1036	#             the request is cleared so it does not re-trigger; cycle CONTINUES.
1037	#   deny    → caller terminates the cycle with blocked_on_scope (NO loop). Covers
1038	#             the default-off case: a non-expandable cycle resolves every request
1039	#             to deny, so a structurally-blocked build abandons cleanly.
1040	#   none    → no request present; cycle proceeds normally.
1041	# The security floor lives in scope-governance.sh and is unbreachable here.
1042	_cycle_resolve_scope_expansion() {
1043	    local cycle_id="$1" state_dir="$2" blob="${3:-}"
1044	    local safe="${cycle_id//-/_}"
1045	    : "$state_dir"
1046	
1047	    # #2189: only a request a member of THIS iteration reported. #1849's run
1048	    # ended when design_verify_cycle (no build member) read build's leftover
1049	    # request from build-summary.json and denied it.
1050	    local req
1051	    req="$(jq -c '[ .[]? | (.report.scope_request // empty)
1052	                  | select(((.files? // []) | length) > 0) ] | first // empty' <<< "${blob:-\{\}}" 2>/dev/null)"
1053	    [[ -z "$req" || "$req" == "null" ]] && { echo "none"; return 0; }
1054	
1055	    # Load the resolver core (idempotent source guard inside the lib).
1056	    local _gov="${_ZBUILD_ROOT:-$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)}/scripts/lib/scope-governance.sh"
1057	    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
1058	    [[ -f "$_gov" ]] && source "$_gov"
1059	    if ! declare -F scope_resolve_request >/dev/null 2>&1; then
1060	        # Resolver unavailable — fail safe to deny (clean abandon, never loop).
1061	        echo "deny"; return 0
1062	    fi
1063	
1064	    local expandable autogrant escalate
1065	    local ev="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_EXPANDABLE_${safe}"; expandable="${!ev:-false}"
1066	    local av="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_AUTO_GRANT_${safe}"; autogrant="${!av:-}"
1067	    local sv="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_ESCALATE_${safe}";   escalate="${!sv:-none}"
1068	
1069	    local decision action
1070	    decision="$(scope_resolve_request "$req" "$expandable" "$autogrant" "$escalate" 2>/dev/null)"
1071	    action="$(jq -r '.action // "deny"' <<<"$decision" 2>/dev/null || echo deny)"
1072	
1073	    if [[ "$action" == "grant" ]]; then
1074	        local grant_file="$state_dir/scope-expansion-grant.txt"
1075	        jq -r '.granted[]?' <<<"$decision" 2>/dev/null > "$grant_file"
1076	        export ZBUILD_SCOPE_EXPANSION_GRANT="$grant_file"
1077	        # The request lives in this iteration's reports only; the next
1078	        # iteration starts from fresh ones, so nothing is cleared (#2189 — the
1079	        # engine used to rewrite build-summary.json here).
1080	        eb_emit_event "cycle.scope.granted" "cycle_id=$cycle_id" \
1081	            "files=$(jq -r '[.granted[]?] | join(",")' <<<"$decision" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null || true
1082	        echo "grant"; return 0
1083	    fi
1084	
1085	    # escalate (v1) and deny both end the cycle cleanly — no loop.
1086	    eb_emit_event "cycle.scope.denied" "cycle_id=$cycle_id" \
1087	        "action=$action" "reason=$(jq -r '.reason // ""' <<<"$decision" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null || true
1088	    echo "deny"; return 0
1089	}
1090	
1091	# ─── _cycle_apply_feedback <iter_next> <state_dir> ──────────────────────────
1092	# Before the next iteration: the targeted-test hand-offs for the test stage.
1093	# (Template feedback wires are retired, ADR-055 §4: every stage reads every
1094	# stage's latest output under Previous work.)
1095	_cycle_apply_feedback() {
1096	    local state_dir="$2"   # $1 (the next iteration) is kept in the call shape
1097	
1098	    # ADR-034 / #846: wire targeted-test artifacts for the next iter's test stage.
1099	    # ZBUILD_TEST_RED_SET  → path to test-red-set.json from the just-completed run.
1100	    # ZBUILD_TEST_CHANGED_FILES → comma-separated files_changed[] from build-summary.json.
1101	    # Both are exported (or unset when absent) so _test_run_inner on iter N+1 can
1102	    # build the targeted set without querying the state dir itself.
1103	    local _tr_red_set="$state_dir/artifacts/test-red-set.json"
1104	    if [[ -f "$_tr_red_set" ]]; then
1105	        export ZBUILD_TEST_RED_SET="$_tr_red_set"
1106	    else
1107	        unset ZBUILD_TEST_RED_SET 2>/dev/null || true
1108	    fi
1109	    # #2189: the files the members of the iteration just finished reported
1110	    # changing — not a stage's file read by name.
1111	    local _changed_csv
1112	    _changed_csv="$(_cycle_reported_changed_files "${_CYCLE_LAST_VERDICTS_BLOB:-}")"
1113	    if [[ -n "$_changed_csv" ]]; then
1114	        export ZBUILD_TEST_CHANGED_FILES="$_changed_csv"
1115	    else
1116	        unset ZBUILD_TEST_CHANGED_FILES 2>/dev/null || true
1117	    fi
1118	
1119	    return 0
1120	}
1121	
1122	# ─── _cycle_state_init <state_file> ──────────────────────────────────────────
1123	# Schema-additive: ensure .cycle_iterations[<cycle_id>] exists. Defensive init
1124	# guards against older state files crashing on `.cycle_iterations` access
1125	# (silent-failure finding #7).
1126	_cycle_state_jq_init() {
1127	    local _now; TZ=UTC0 printf -v _now '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1
1128	    jq --arg id "$_ZB_CYCLE_ID" \
1129	       --arg history "$_ZB_CYCLE_HISTORY" \
1130	       --argjson max "$_ZB_CYCLE_MAX" \
1131	       --arg now "$_now" \
1132	       '(.cycle_iterations //= {})
1133	        | (.cycle_iterations[$id] //= {
1134	            status: "in_progress",
1135	            current_iter: 0,
1136	            max_iterations: $max,
1137	            history_file: $history,
1138	            iter: []
1139	          })
1140	        | .updated_at = $now'
1141	}
1142	
1143	_cycle_state_init() {
1144	    local state_file="$1" cycle_id="$2" history_file="$3" max_iter="$4"
1145	    export _ZB_CYCLE_ID="$cycle_id" _ZB_CYCLE_HISTORY="$history_file" \
1146	           _ZB_CYCLE_MAX="$max_iter"
1147	    locked_state_update "$state_file" "_cycle_state_jq_init" || return 1
1148	    unset _ZB_CYCLE_ID _ZB_CYCLE_HISTORY _ZB_CYCLE_MAX
1149	}
1150	
1151	# ─── _cycle_state_write_iter_atomic ──────────────────────────────────────────
1152	# Single atomic write per iter boundary (silent-failure finding #12).
1153	# Updates: current_iter, iter[] append, status. NEVER split.
1154	_cycle_state_jq_write_iter() {
1155	    local _now; TZ=UTC0 printf -v _now '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1
1156	    jq --arg id "$_ZB_CYCLE_ID" \
1157	       --argjson n "$_ZB_CYCLE_N" \
1158	       --arg verdict "$_ZB_CYCLE_VERDICT" \
1159	       --arg status "$_ZB_CYCLE_ITER_STATUS" \
1160	       --argjson fc "$_ZB_CYCLE_FC" \
1161	       --arg overall "$_ZB_CYCLE_OVERALL" \
1162	       --arg now "$_now" \
1163	       '(.cycle_iterations //= {})
1164	        | (.cycle_iterations[$id] //= {iter:[]})
1165	        | .cycle_iterations[$id].current_iter = $n
1166	        | .cycle_iterations[$id].status = $overall
1167	        | .cycle_iterations[$id].iter += [{
1168	              n: $n,
1169	              status: $status,
1170	              verdict: $verdict,
1171	              failure_count: $fc,
1172	              ended_at: $now
1173	          }]
1174	        | .updated_at = $now'
1175	}
1176	
1177	_cycle_state_write_iter_atomic() {
1178	    local state_file="$1" cycle_id="$2" n="$3" verdict="$4" iter_status="$5" \
1179	          failure_count="$6" overall_status="$7"
1180	    export _ZB_CYCLE_ID="$cycle_id" _ZB_CYCLE_N="$n" \
1181	           _ZB_CYCLE_VERDICT="$verdict" _ZB_CYCLE_ITER_STATUS="$iter_status" \
1182	           _ZB_CYCLE_FC="$failure_count" _ZB_CYCLE_OVERALL="$overall_status"
1183	    locked_state_update "$state_file" "_cycle_state_jq_write_iter" || return 1
1184	    unset _ZB_CYCLE_ID _ZB_CYCLE_N _ZB_CYCLE_VERDICT _ZB_CYCLE_ITER_STATUS \
1185	          _ZB_CYCLE_FC _ZB_CYCLE_OVERALL
1186	}
1187	
1188	# ─── _cycle_state_write_member_atomic ────────────────────────────────────────
1189	# Persists a cycle member's terminal status and classified verdict into the
1190	# top-level stage_statuses / stage_verdicts maps of pipeline-state.json.
1191	# Uses locked_state_update (same pattern as _cycle_state_write_iter_atomic).
1192	# All call sites use || true — a lock failure must never abort a cycle iter.
1193	_cycle_state_jq_write_member() {
1194	    local _now; TZ=UTC0 printf -v _now '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1
1195	    jq --arg s "$_ZB_CYCLE_MEMBER" \
1196	       --arg st "$_ZB_CYCLE_MEMBER_STATUS" \
1197	       --arg v "$_ZB_CYCLE_MEMBER_VERDICT" \
1198	       --arg now "$_now" \
1199	       '(.stage_statuses //= {}) | .stage_statuses[$s] = $st
1200	        | (.stage_verdicts //= {}) | .stage_verdicts[$s] = $v
1201	        | .updated_at = $now'
1202	}
1203	
1204	_cycle_state_write_member_atomic() {
1205	    local state_file="$1" member="$2" status="$3" verdict="$4"
1206	    export _ZB_CYCLE_MEMBER="$member" \
1207	           _ZB_CYCLE_MEMBER_STATUS="$status" \
1208	           _ZB_CYCLE_MEMBER_VERDICT="$verdict"
1209	    locked_state_update "$state_file" "_cycle_state_jq_write_member" || return 1
1210	    unset _ZB_CYCLE_MEMBER _ZB_CYCLE_MEMBER_STATUS _ZB_CYCLE_MEMBER_VERDICT
1211	}
1212	
1213	# ─── _cycle_iter_dispatch <iter> <state_file> ────────────────────────────────
